title: Čech-to-derived
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site with fibre products, $X\in\Ob(\mathcal C)$
and $\mathfrak U=\{U_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ a family of morphisms generating a covering
sieve of $X$. For an abelian sheaf $F$ on $\mathcal C$ there is a first-quadrant spectral sequence

$$
E_2^{p,q}=\Cech^p\bigl(\mathfrak U,\ \mathcal H^q(F)\bigr)
\ \Longrightarrow\ H^{p+q}(X,F),
$$

where $\mathcal H^q(F)$ is the presheaf $V\mapsto H^q(V,F)$.

proof.text: Use the small-site convention in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]: objects, morphisms, covering indices and the coefficient groups are sets in a common universe. This is Stacks Tag 00VI (sites.tex, remark-no-big-sites), not an additional geometric assumption. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives], choose an injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$ in $\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ as in [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. In particular the resolution is on $\mathcal C$, not an unintroduced sheaf on $\mathcal C/X$. Compute $H^q(V,F)$ using this resolution and evaluation at $V$, as in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. The Ext formulation in the column and total comparison statements is taken in this common universe and means these same resolution-computed groups; no large-site or independent coefficient-universe assertion is being used.

source.place: Step 1 (choice of resolution); Stacks sites.tex Tag 00VI, remark-no-big-sites, and injectives.tex Tag 01DP, theorem-sheaves-injectives

proof.text:
Form the specified double complex of [def-sc-cech-resolution-double-complex],
$$D^{p,q}=C^p(\mathfrak U,I^q)=\prod_{(i_0,\ldots,i_p)\in I^{p+1}}I^q(U_{i_0}\times_X\cdots\times_XU_{i_p}).$$
Here the horizontal maps are the alternating sums of the omitted-factor restrictions and the vertical maps come from $I^\bullet$. They commute by the naturality stipulated in that construction. The given fibre products supply every finite wide pullback over $X$ (the empty one is $X$), and successive binary fibre products supply the products of tuples in $\mathcal C/X$; no terminal object of $\mathcal C$ is required. Use the first-quadrant total complex with $d=d_I+(-1)^p d_{II}$ from [def-sp-double-complex-total]. In degree $n$ its sum has only $0\le p\le n$, so this totalization has no infinite-diagonal issue.

source.place: Opening paragraph and Step 1 (specified double complex and its totalization)

proof.text:
Apply [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] to this first-quadrant double complex in abelian groups. Its first filtration gives a spectral sequence with
$$E_1^{p,q}=H^q(D^{p,\bullet}),\qquad E_2^{p,q}=H^p\bigl(H^q_{II}(D)\bigr),$$
where $d_1$ is induced by the horizontal differential. It abuts to $H^{p+q}(\operatorname{Tot}D)$ with a finite decreasing filtration in each total degree. Thus the page identification requires an isomorphism of the horizontal complexes of vertical cohomology, not just unrelated isomorphisms of their individual terms.

source.place: Step 1 (two filtrations), and Step 2 (first spectral sequence)

proof.text:
For the same $I$, $X$ and family, apply [lem-sc-cech-resolution-columns]. Its statement identifies the entire complex $H^q_{II}(D)$ with $C^\bullet(\mathfrak U,\mathcal H^q(F))$, including the horizontal differential. Hence the preceding $E_1$ is the Cech cochain complex in degree $p$, and taking its $p$-th cohomology gives
$$E_2^{p,q}\cong\check H^p(\mathfrak U,\mathcal H^q(F)).$$
The last equality is the definition of Cech cohomology in [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]. The column lemma works for an arbitrary family; consequently its hypotheses require neither an acyclic cover nor a vanishing hypothesis on $F$. It includes the product-cohomology and evaluation comparisons, so no assertion about preservation of injectives under localization is needed here.

source.place: Step 2 (column cohomology and the Cech horizontal differential)

proof.text:
Now use the covering hypothesis: the sieve generated by $\mathfrak U$ belongs to the site's topology. For this same resolution and double complex, [lem-sc-cech-resolution-total] gives, for every $n\ge0$, an isomorphism
$$\theta_n:H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^n(X,F).$$
This is precisely the total-cohomology comparison required by Step 3 of the unit, whose argument uses injective Cech row acyclicity (Stacks sites-cohomology.tex, Tags 03F6 and 03AW). The cited total-comparison statement has the covering-sieve hypothesis, so no replacement of a sieve-generating family by a finite, open, or affine covering is involved.

source.place: Step 3 (total cohomology and the abutment); Stacks sites-cohomology.tex Tags 03F6, lemma-injective-abelian-sheaf-injective-presheaf, and 03AW, lemma-injective-trivial-cech

proof.text: Let $T^aH^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)$ be the image filtration given by the double-complex theorem. Define $F^aH^n(X,F)=\theta_n(T^aH^n(\operatorname{Tot}D))$. Since $\theta_n$ is an isomorphism, this is a decreasing filtration with $F^0H^n(X,F)=H^n(X,F)$ and $F^{n+1}H^n(X,F)=0$; it induces isomorphisms of successive quotients with those of $T$. Their identifications with $E_\infty^{a,n-a}$ therefore give an abutment in exactly the sense of [sk-def-groth-ss]. Combining this filtration with the second-page identification above proves the claimed spectral sequence. This spells out the transfer of the abutment instead of assuming an unspecified compatibility between two filtrations.

source.place: Step 4 (combine the page and abutment calculations)

proof.text: For the optional collapse stated in Step 4 of the unit, suppose $\mathcal H^q(F)=0$ for $q>0$. All rows of $E_2$ except $q=0$ vanish, while $\mathcal H^0(F)=F$ by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Every differential $d_r$ with $r\ge2$ to or from $(n,0)$ has a zero source or target, so $E_\infty^{n,0}=\check H^n(\mathfrak U,F)$. The abutment filtration of [sk-def-groth-ss] then has zero successive quotients except in degree $n$: $F^0=\cdots=F^n=H^n(X,F)$ and $F^{n+1}=0$. Thus the edge identification is an isomorphism $\check H^n(\mathfrak U,F)\cong H^n(X,F)$. This is a consequence of the sequence just constructed, not an extra hypothesis of the theorem.

source.place: Step 4 (optional row-zero collapse); Stacks sites-cohomology.tex Tag 03AZ, lemma-cech-spectral-sequence
